items.a: **internal biology matched to external cycles; melatonin** tracks day length (less light → more/longer melatonin → lower winter energy for most people).

items.q: What should you remember about **Circadian precision matters**?
items.a: **view 10–30 min bright light (ideally sun)** within ~1 h of waking + again afternoon/evening; minimize evening bright light; exercise at consistent times.

items.q: What should you remember about **Ashoff isolation studies**?
items.a: **disrupted circadian entrainment breaks** both long- and short-interval time judgment → impairs work performance.

items.q: What should you remember about **90-min ultradian focus**?
items.a: **brain can focus ~90 min then acetylcholine/dopamine** circuits resist further deep engagement; you choose when a cycle starts (not tied to sleep-cycle end).

items.q: What should you remember about **Max ~2 hard 90-min blocks/day**?
items.a: **separate by 2–4 h; not email/social** — hard problem solving; one block still feels taxing.

items.q: What should you remember about **Dopamine speeds the clock**?
items.a: **higher dopamine → think** more time passed than actually did.

items.q: What should you remember about **Serotonin slows the clock**?
items.a: **opposite direction; evening serotonin** rise supports sleep transition (cross-link meal timing focus and sleep).

items.q: What should you remember about **Do hardest task early**?
items.a: **supported by circadian neuromodulator literature, not just psychology.**

items.q: What should you remember about **Sleep disruption**?
What should you remember about **Trauma memory = rate code**?
items.a: **hippocampus stores both which neurons fired and** at what rate; over-clocking makes memories hard to shake even when emotions eventually decouple with treatment.

items.q: What should you remember about **Amusement park paradox**?
items.a: **kids' exciting day flies** by live, expands in memory months later.

items.q: What should you remember about **Novelty density**?
items.a: **three apartments + 3× people +** 3× experiences in NYC → feel you've lived there longer than one apartment/year.
